question: A 14-year-old girl comes to the physician for exertional leg pain. The pain began last week when she started jogging to lose weight. She is at the 5th percentile for height and 80th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows a broad neck with bilateral excess skin folds that extend to the shoulders, as well as a low-set hairline and ears. There is an increased carrying angle when she fully extends her arms at her sides. Pulses are palpable in all extremities; lower leg pulses are delayed. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Exertional leg pain" -> "Started jogging to lose weight" -> "5th percentile for height, 80th percentile for weight" -> "Broad neck with bilateral excess skin folds, low-set hairline and ears, increased carrying angle" -> "Possible Turner syndrome" -> "Additional finding: Ovarian dysgenesis" -> 70%

enhanced_information: In a 14-year-old girl with exertional leg pain, broad neck, low-set hairline and ears, and increased carrying angle, the most likely additional finding is ovarian dysgenesis, consistent with Turner syndrome.
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 14-year-old girl is suggestive of Turner syndrome, characterized by short stature, webbed neck, low-set ears, and a wide carrying angle. The delayed lower leg pulses may indicate coarctation of the aorta, a common cardiovascular anomaly associated with Turner syndrome. One of the hallmark features of Turner syndrome is ovarian dysgenesis, leading to primary amenorrhea and infertility. The other options, such as absent uterus, mitral valve prolapse, triphalangeal thumb, and horseshoe adrenal gland, are not typically associated with Turner syndrome.
